review:
VGH... What is there to say?

I know that Obsidian were locked into having to do POE, but man, THIS is what they should have lead with. 

Tyranny is better than Pillars 1 and 2 in everything important, by a wide margin. The world, the story, the characters, the artstyle, the tone, the themes, the combat, the RPG mechanics, the exploration, the itemization, the choice and consequences...

What could have been... What we lost...
Underrated game that gives many realistic choices to work through that create introspection during roleplay and investment in the story.

通关后的情感很复杂，能明显感到一周目是远远不足以窥见这款游戏的完整世界观的，四只手数不清的各个势力、性格迥异的大量主要角色，也许黑岛的野心比我所预想的大很多。或许这款游戏没有[url=store.steampowered.com/app/291650/Pillars_of_Eternity/] 永恒之柱 [/url]对哲学与社会的思辨，或许没有[url=store.steampowered.com/app/466300/Planescape_Torment_Enhanced_Edition] 异域镇魂曲 [/url]对存在与死亡的思考，但架不住自定义法术和释放足以改写现实的伟大赦令真的很好玩......等DLC打折肯定会找时间体验二周目的，我会将这款游戏推荐给所有轻量级CRPG玩家，如果其他老派CRPG让你打怵，试试这个。前提是你可以忍受那种“三部曲直接上来游玩第二部”的奇妙断层感，但这对我来说反倒是加分项。

不过这游戏很有趣地体现出了战争中士兵和上级的作用——尼拉特不上战场整天折磨队友；艾休老年痴呆日渐衰弱也打不动架；马克和屠农更是杂种城法庭大门不迈，不屈者和青铜兄弟会甚至都比你们强。所有人想一出是一出，想用生命效忠谁也随便改口。本质上，我甚至猜测凯洛斯在最初征服这片土地时压根没带多少士兵，打到哪就收当地的子弟兵。难道说，凯洛斯其实是真猩红歌者？！

所谓帝国，其实非常不像一个高度中央集权国家。不屈者是一个军阀集团，歌者是一个恐怖组织，青铜兄弟会是雇佣兵，杂种城是自治城邦，各种法官和执政官各有私人势力。这很反常，整个帝国更像凯洛斯建立的巨大封建联盟。凯洛斯真正控制的是合法性本身，大家并非忠于帝国，而是忠于各地领主、各自部族，然后这些人共同承认凯洛斯。“昨天还是敌人，今天就宣誓效忠”，嗯，还是蛮少见的，至少我的游戏体验里是这样的。

这其实也是这款游戏的一种很特别的反英雄主义——传统奇幻世界观中大将军冲锋陷阵、宰相运筹帷幄、国王统御全局，但这款游戏中他们越来越像国家机器里的部门主管，给我一种帝国已经老了的感觉。我——主角缚命官——才是真正上战场的人，我看游戏名别叫暴君了，改名叫天皇吧。

结局，或许也没那么突兀？从演出效果上来讲，凯洛斯的铁蹄数量不会少，而主角这边也掌握着藐厌军或歌者的军队，正面大战场并不适合等角视角的表现形式。何况这是一场必赢的战争，凯洛斯的军队不过是茫茫野草罢了，打起来只会觉得厌烦。非要说哪里遗憾，或许是诸多问题没能解释得清，凯洛斯身世如何啊，谁建立了五座尖塔和古城墙啊，赦令的本质、帝君统治前的世界是什么样、石冢叛变的真正原因......或许其他路线能够解释，这让我更有必要二周目了。

当你终于拥有改写世界规则的力量之后，你会成为第二个凯洛斯吗？

如果没有凯洛斯，这个世界真的会更好吗？

凯洛斯究竟是问题本身，还是对更大混乱的一种回答？

也许最后能汇聚成一句总结......只有“黑岛牛逼”四个大字。

Но. Как обычно, им не хватило времени, чтобы всё это действительно заработало. Контент скатывается чуть ли не после первого акта, на лицо куча дыр и недоделок. Из четырёх основных путей прохождения хорошо проработаны только два. 
То же самое и по части геймплея - сразу видно, что игра формировалась вокруг системы создания заклинаний. Но даже она сделана наполовину. Баланс между школами магии отсутствует напрочь, некоторые ветки вообще бесполезны. 
Уровни сложности сделаны по шутерному типу - на высоком у врагов просто выкручено ХП и резисты. Всё. Всех боссов вы будете тупо забивать чистым уроном, ибо никакие дебаффы на них не действуют.

From a gameplay standpoint, it was a tough pill to swallow. Including one particular [spoiler]Azure Shield[/spoiler] game-ending bug. The only thing that kept me going was treating it like an interactive book, one that leaves a bitter aftertaste. And I don't know exactly why. Maybe it had outstayed its welcome and the flaws got me in the end, or it's THAT good it got under my skin. Perhaps both. Alas. Either way, my final judgment, like the Edict of Malediction, will remain.

I would give this a sideways thumb if I could.  I like the basic idea that you are in service to the bad guy, and can choose to be either Darth Vader evil or somewhat decent and make decisions based on that.  But the story writing isn't great.  I was so annoyed that I (as basically a legal clerk) had to do an entire army's work for them.  What are they even there for?  I also didn't find the characters to be memorable or noteworthy.

Practically, I found the puzzles to be incredibly boring (collect X stones or rubbings, etc), and the layout of the various levels was very annoying.  I often had to wait a long time while my characters ran a winding route just to get back to the spot where they could hit the exit.  And then there were the times when I had to wait for them to run to something like a rope, click on the rope, and then wait for them to run to the exit.  It eventually got frustrating enough that I dropped the game entirely.  I also didn't find the combat interesting or fun.  It's just okay.

I picked up Tyranny for the simplest reason: it looked damn good. The interface, the art, the whole visual package. Played it in 2018, a couple years after launch, and honestly the presentation still impressed me. Voice acting? Solid. No complaints there. The people behind this game clearly gave a damn about polish.

Here's where it fell apart for me, though. Tyranny's big thing is the Edict timer. You get a task, and you get a countdown in days. Finish it or face the consequences. Cool concept on paper. In practice, it made me feel like I was doing homework with a deadline instead of playing a game I paid for.

I kept thinking "I should check that side area" and then remembering the clock was ticking. That tension is intentional, I know. Some people probably thrive on it. I just wanted to take my time with this world that looked so good, and the game kept telling me I couldn't.

If countdown pressure sounds fun to you, give it a shot. The foundation is solid. It just wasn't my kind of RPG.

[h3][i]Tyranny[/i] is a CRPG with a unique premise: What would you do if you worked for the bad guys who were about to take over the world?[/h3]

[h2]What I liked:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Morality was handled in a very unique way.
[*]The spell-crafting system is unique and engaging.
[*]Artifact powers add a lot of build variety.
[*]Lore and worldbuilding are done very well.
[*]The companions felt believable and impactful. I liked their quests as well.
[*]Very few instances of railroading. you were mostly free to do things in whatever order you liked.
[*]Several of the pre-rendered backgrounds, especially the more grandiose ones, were truly awe-inspiring.
[*]Though the game is not fully voice acted, the parts that we got were really well done.
[*]The progression system provided a great power fantasy.
[*]Most of the important characters had cool character models and were written very well. I loved the Voices of Nerat and Tunon the Adjudicator. 
[*]Most people dislike that the story [spoiler]kind of ends on a cliffhanger[/spoiler], but I think it was a great way to end it. 
[*]Most of your choices have impactful consequences.
[/list]

[h2]What I'm neutral on:[/h2]
[list]
[*]The real time with pause combat felt like a worse version of that of Pillars of Eternity.
[*]The graphics are not good.
[*]The inventory management could have been better. It felt clunky at times.
[/list]

[h2]What I disliked:[/h2]
[list]
[*]The sound design for combat was horrible. Very little feedback for spells and abilities made them feel like there was no weight to them.
[*]The writing could be a bit flowery for my taste at times - not as much as Pillars of Eternity, though.
[*]Many of the boss fights didn't feel unique enough at normal difficulty.
[*]The order in which the ending slides were presented made a few of them feel a bit redundant.
[/list]

Overall, I highly recommend playing [i]Tyranny[/i]. It's shorter than most CRPGs of similar quality, and there's so much choice and consequence that you cannot see everything in one playthrough. These two things together make for a highly replayable game. [h3]8.5/10[/h3]

A short and sweet CRPG from Obsidian. It carries the Pillars of Eternity DNA and feels similar, but still starkly different. The game has amazing world-building and one of the best, or perhaps even *the* best, player-character responses in the genre. It's one of the few games that doesn't try to put your character down just so it can elevate some random OC pet NPC of the developers.

The narrative is tight and neat. There are 4 distinct paths you can follow, each having drastically different outcomes for the world.

So the positives:
* excellent narrative
* spellcrafting is fun (being a mage as a whole is by far the best in this game)
* great choices
* good replayability
* doesn't overstay its welcome
* Conquest, as a start, is a novel and amazing idea. I wish more games would do this
* unique setting with a believable world and characters in it

negatives:
* lacks polish (everything feels somewhat half-baked: the sound equalization, the lack of portraits, randomly having no VA for important situations in the middle of a conversation, etc.)
* terrible main character progression (while the talent trees for companions are good, the main character tree is one of the weakest things I've seen in a CRPG - oh wow, my party can now switch weapons faster :P)
* terrible RPG progression as a whole... narrow range of items and almost no build variety. If it weren't for the spellcrafting mechanic, this would be the worst character building I've seen in a modern CRPG
* real-time with pause just doesn't work for this game. I found myself having to pause every second - at that point, just make it turn-based
* little to no enemy variety. We have humans (two different styles, either aggressive or defensive, with substyles like rogue, mage, warrior) and banes (with about 5 different styles - or colors - all of which feel the same). That's it. No other enemies...
* worst DLC I've played in my life. Bastard's Wound is an unfinished, buggy mess that still hasn't been fixed after 10+ years, and it almost made me quit the game.

Overall, Tyranny is a unique game that I can recommend, but it would work better as a choose-your-own-adventure-style game than a CRPG, as it lacks CRPG depth in terms of character building.

Tyranny is not a great game, but I lowkey kinda love it. If you have read The Black Company by Glen Cook, and you should they are excellent fantasy novels, you're basically playing as the strongest of the Taken. Which means, you're the baddies. At first, I really hated that, but then I read the Black Company, and it's actually a great idea.

When I first played Tyranny, I did not like the game and some of those dislikes remain. The combat is largely a carry-over from Pillars of Eternity, but thankfully Obsidian learned about UX/UI design and the interface is better. Still not great, but better. They also massively simplified being a spellcaster and the spell-building system is neat. It's still Real-Time with Pause, which may not be to your taste, but it's less baffling that PoE1.

The real thing about Tyranny that I think a lot of people didn't like is that you are playing as the baddies. If you, like me, cut your cRPG teeth on Dragon Age or Knights of the Old Republic, you may be expecting that it will be or become a heroic fantasy. Yeah, no, it doesn't. You're the bad guy and you stay the bad guy the whole time. What you get to decide is what kind of bad guy. This is a controversial choice, but I think it's actually a really genius decision from Obsidian and it's really what has kept me playing.

Tyranny is the perfect length for an RPG. 

If you're somebody who has nothing to do but play games for 12 hours a day I can see why you would think this is too short, but for somebody with a life this is an amazingly paced RPG. One of the few that doesn't get too repetitive by the end.

The story is dramatic and fluid. There is very little meaningless meandering, everything feeds into an epic, dramatic narrative and it doesn't drag at all. Other RPGs have a problem where your build takes a long time to come online and then it just sort of stagnates. You just get a stronger version of what you had before, it just gets boring. In this game once you reach that point it starts to wrap up, and rather than giving you a bunch of generic hordes to fight, you get a series of unique fights and an ending with player-agency. 

And here's the thing about the choice-making in this game. It matters way more than in most games, because the narrative is focused and there are certain important moments that can play out one of a couple ways. Many seemingly small decisions feed into these moments and so they make the way you roleplay overall feel important. 

You can also branch the story in very significant ways during key moments. They're the same 3-4 ways, but you can do the branching at multiple different points in the game, transforming the way events play out, which is only possible because the game is not 100+ hours long with tons of filler-like locations to slog through. 

Like BG3 is a really fun game, but the vast majority of choices are just for flavour. There's almost no significant branching in the story, because how the hell can there be when the game is 100+ hours long? Tyranny makes it matter in a way that other games can't due to overinflated length and scope.

Overall this is the best-paced RPG I've ever played. It has awesome art, fun gameplay (for once I don't hate the RTwP combat in a CRPG), epic atmosphere, great world-building and is overall a memorable and unique RPG experience.

I wouldn't recommend it based on what I like to play but it is what is advertised and a solid game.
For that reason I will recommend it ON SALE.

Even then it's overpriced in that you can get a better game like Dragons Age 1 at the same price if not better (on sale) but if you want an RPG to play for consequences definitely have this on your wishlist.
